sections.html:
No county in South Dakota has more people. Minnehaha sits on the eastern border with Minnesota, and Sioux Falls, the state's biggest city, is the county seat. The Big Sioux River winds south-southeast through the east-central part. About 814 square miles of rolling farmland, with lakes and ponds in the west, make up the county, and the name comes from a Sioux word for rapid water or waterfall.

The 2020 census counted 197,214 residents. For 2019 to 2023 the median home value was $266,600, and 64 percent of homes are owner-occupied. Besides Sioux Falls, the incorporated places are Baltic, Brandon, Colton, Crooks, Dell Rapids, Garretson, Hartford and Valley Springs.

Health care employs the most people, led by Sanford Health and Avera Health, with the school district, Smithfield Foods, Amazon, Hy-Vee and the big banks behind them. A rental or inherited house here competes in a metro market, and a cash offer can matter most when a property needs work that a retail buyer's lender wouldn't finance.

sections.h2: Where to go and who to call
sections.html:
Equalization values the property, the Treasurer collects the tax, and the Register of Deeds records the sale. The Auditor figures the tax from the budgets that elected officials set.

  • Treasurer: 415 N. Dakota Ave., Sioux Falls, SD 57104. Open 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on weekdays except legal holidays. Phone (605) 367-4211.
  • Director of Equalization: (605) 367-4228. Handles assessed values and owner-occupied status. The Treasurer has no say over assessments.
  • Register of Deeds: 415 N. Dakota Ave., first floor, open 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

The Treasurer's counter is busiest on Mondays and Fridays, on the first business day of the month and the last two, and the day after a holiday. For a closing-week payment, pick a quieter day.

The tax year starts January 1. You may pay the first half without penalty through April 30 and the second half through October 31. Whatever is unpaid on May 1 or November 1 is delinquent, and a late payment carries a 10% annual penalty, which works out to .83333% per month.

A payment counts as late unless it is postmarked by April 30 or October 31, and online payments count on the date of the transaction. When a deadline lands on a weekend or holiday, pay by 4:45 p.m. on the last working day. The drop box and online payments work until midnight. The office takes no early payments and gives no early-payment discount. State law, SDCL 10-21-23, uses the same delinquency dates.

  • Mail: 415 N. Dakota Ave., Sioux Falls, SD 57104, with the statement stub or the address, parcel number or bill number. Without one of those, the payment is returned.
  • Drop box: outside the west doors of the County Administration Building, open around the clock.
  • Online: a 2.35% convenience fee appears as a separate charge, and posting can take 7 to 10 business days.
  • Late balances can't be paid online. Call (605) 367-4211.
  • Checks need a pre-printed, in-state name and address.

November 1 is the legal assessment date every year, and the property's condition that day sets the assessment for the year after. A house half built on November 1 is assessed at half. Residential land is commonly valued by front footage and acreages by the acre. Buildings are judged on quality, size, design and condition, and a finished basement adds value.

Appraisers get a copy of each building permit from a city or the county planning office and review those properties. Routine upkeep, like a new roof or siding, usually doesn't change the assessment. For a rough estimate of a new project's effect, the county suggests taking the cost, labor included, and multiplying by the current tax rate.

Taxable value is 85% of full and true value. Each taxing unit divides its unfunded budget by the taxable value in its area to find its levy. Owner-occupied homes form a separate class: you must own and occupy the home on November 1, and a new owner applies between November 1 and March 15.

Call the Director of Equalization first, since an appraiser can review the property. For a formal appeal, the county publishes an Appeal Process Guide. A written appeal goes to the local board, which for Sioux Falls residents is the city's Local Board of Equalization, or to the county board.

StepUsual date
Written appeal to local board clerkAround March 13 (postmark counts)
Local board meetsMid to late March
Appeal to county auditorApril 1
County board of equalization sitsApril 8 to 29
Letter to Office of Hearing ExaminersMid May
Circuit court appealWithin 30 days of notice

Dates move a little each year, so confirm them with the county. Minnehaha County hearings take place in the Commission Chambers on the third floor at 415 N. Dakota Ave. You can't take the same dispute to the hearing examiners and circuit court at once.

Recording a deed costs $30, and the state transfer fee is $1.00 per thousand, or $0.50 per $500 of value. SDCL 43-4-21 sets the transfer fee, and it applies to deeds only when there is consideration.

  • Documents over 50 pages add $2.00 per extra page.
  • Copies are $1.00 per page, and certification is $5.00.
  • A plat is $60 and a master deed is $75.
  • A federal tax lien or its release is $20, while a state tax lien is recorded free.

The Register of Deeds doesn't give legal advice, so have a title company or attorney prepare the deed.

When taxes are due at the same time as a sale, the Treasurer's payoff figure drives the closing statement. Call (605) 367-4211 for it, since late balances can't be paid online. The unpaid amount is paid from your proceeds at closing.

Check the calendar before you pick a closing date. A sale in late April has to deal with a first half about to turn delinquent, and a sale in October faces the second. We buy Minnehaha County houses as-is and can work from the payoff number, including houses that need repairs or have tenants.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Minnehaha County?
faqs.a: The tax year starts January 1. The first half is accepted without penalty through April 30 and the second half through October 31, and unpaid halves turn delinquent on May 1 and November 1.

faqs.q: What is the penalty for paying Minnehaha County taxes late?
faqs.a: A 10% annual penalty, or .83333% per month. A mailed payment counts as on time only if it is postmarked by April 30 or October 31.

faqs.q: Who sets my Minnehaha County property value?
faqs.a: The Director of Equalization, not the Treasurer. Call (605) 367-4228 about values, owner-occupied status and appeals. The legal assessment date is November 1.

faqs.q: How much is the South Dakota transfer fee on a home sale?
faqs.a: It is $0.50 per $500 of value, or $1.00 per $1,000, collected when the deed is recorded. Recording the deed itself costs $30 in Minnehaha County.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Minnehaha County house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The Treasurer can give you a payoff figure, and the balance is paid from the sale proceeds at closing. Delinquent taxes can't be paid online, so call the office.
